name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
benefit: ₹6,000 per year in three ₹2,000 instalments, paid directly to the bank account (DBT).
eligibility_summary: Landowning farmer families (husband, wife and minor children count as one family), subject to exclusions: institutional landholders, current/former holders of constitutional posts, (retired) government employees and pensioners drawing ₹10,000+ a month (Group D/MTS excepted), income-tax payers, and registered doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs and architects.
how_to_apply: Register on the PM-KISAN portal or through a Common Service Centre or your village revenue officer. e-KYC is mandatory (OTP on the portal, or biometric at a CSC).
source_note: pmkisan.gov.in (e-KYC) and a secondary 2026 summary for the exclusion list

name: PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana)
benefit: Insurance against crop loss from natural calamities, pests and disease. Farmer pays 2% of the sum insured (Kharif food grains/oilseeds), 1.5% (Rabi), up to 5% (commercial/horticultural crops); the government pays the rest.
eligibility_summary: Farmers growing a notified crop in a notified area, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers (with a tenancy document or certificate as your state requires). Loanee and non-loanee farmers can both enrol.
how_to_apply: On pmfby.gov.in (Farmer Corner), or at a bank branch, PACS, Common Service Centre or insurer office, before the enrolment cut-off.
source_note: Drishti IAS (Sept 2026) and a 2026 PMFBY guide; cut-off dates are typical (about 31 July Kharif, 31 December Rabi) and differ by state and crop

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
benefit: Short-term farm credit. Crop loans up to ₹3 lakh carry 7% interest with a 3% government subvention, about 4% effective if repaid on time; the crop-loan limit can go up to ₹5 lakh; loans up to ₹2 lakh need no collateral. Check the current terms with your bank.
eligibility_summary: Owner-cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, and SHGs/JLGs of farmers; also covers animal husbandry and fisheries.
how_to_apply: Apply at any bank branch or PACS (many banks also accept applications online).

name: Soil Health Card Scheme
benefit: Free soil testing with crop-wise nutrient and fertilizer recommendations.
how_to_apply: Ask your local agriculture department or Krishi Vigyan Kendra to collect soil samples from your field.
source_note: Carried over from the earlier version; not re-checked against a 2026 source

name: PM-KUSUM (Solar Pumps & Grid-Connected Solar)
benefit: Subsidy on solar irrigation pumps and support for small solar plants on farm land. The central and state shares differ by state, so ask your state agency for the rate that applies to you.
eligibility_summary: Individual farmers, farmer groups, cooperatives and panchayats with land for the installation. Application windows are run by state nodal agencies.
how_to_apply: Through your state's nodal agency or discom portal; open windows differ by state.
source_note: News reports that the timeline for select projects was extended to March 2027; rules and subsidy rates were not re-verified. Treat as 'check with your state agency'

name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
benefit: Online trading platform linking mandis for transparent price discovery and easier sale across mandis.
eligibility_summary: Farmers who sell through an APMC mandi that is integrated with e-NAM. Final approval comes from your local mandi.
how_to_apply: Register as a farmer on enam.gov.in or the e-NAM app, choose your nearest mandi, and upload your documents for the mandi to verify.

name: PMKSY – Per Drop More Crop (micro-irrigation)
benefit: Subsidy on drip and sprinkler systems: 55% of the indicative unit cost for small and marginal farmers, 45% for other farmers. Some states add more.
eligibility_summary: Farmers installing drip or sprinkler irrigation. 'Small and marginal' means up to 2 hectares (about 4.9 acres) in total. State rules and unit costs vary.
how_to_apply: Through your state horticulture or agriculture department (many states run an online portal).
source_note: PIB press release for the subsidy rates

name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
benefit: Loans for post-harvest and farm infrastructure (warehouses, cold storage, processing, sorting and grading) with 3% interest subvention on loans up to ₹2 crore for up to 7 years, a credit guarantee on loans up to ₹2 crore, and a repayment moratorium of 6 months to 2 years. The scheme runs to 2032-33.
eligibility_summary: Farmers, FPOs, PACS, marketing and multipurpose cooperatives, SHGs/JLGs, agri-entrepreneurs and start-ups, with a bankable project.
how_to_apply: Apply through a participating bank on the AIF portal with a project report.
documents: Land or lease papers for the site

name: National Food Security Mission (NFSM)
benefit: Subsidised seed, farm machinery and inputs to raise rice, wheat, pulses and coarse-cereal production in target districts.
eligibility_summary: Farmers in notified districts growing the mission's target crops. We don't have the district list, so confirm locally.
how_to_apply: Through your district agriculture office or block agriculture officer.
source_note: Carried over from the earlier version; not re-checked against a 2026 source, so the scheme's current structure may have changed

name: Formation & Promotion of 10,000 FPOs
benefit: For a new Farmer Producer Organisation: matching equity grant of ₹2,000 per member up to ₹15 lakh, a credit guarantee for loans up to ₹2 crore, and handholding support (including an operational grant over 3 years).
eligibility_summary: Groups of farmers forming an FPO: at least 300 members in the plains, 100 in hilly and North-Eastern areas. Formation is done through designated implementing agencies; the scheme's target period runs to 2027-28.
how_to_apply: Ask your district agriculture office or an implementing agency (for example NABARD or SFAC) about FPO formation in your area.
documents: Aadhaar and land details of members
source_note: Vision IAS scheme summary; whether new FPO registrations are currently being accepted was not confirmed
